status: COLOSSUS FINAL REEL / ADVANCE COPY SOURCE

entries.caption:
We thought it was a dead world.

No atmosphere.
No rotation.
No measurable heat.

Then another planet passed too close.

The surface opened.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-005
entries.pinned_comment:
ANALYSIS NOTE:

The debris is not orbiting the object.

It is moving inward.

Nothing has escaped the pull.

entries.caption:
It passed Earth without slowing.

No signal.
No reaction.
No sign we mattered.

Then the course changed.

Less than one degree.

New orientation: Earth.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-006
entries.pinned_comment:
ANALYSIS NOTE:

Recorded course correction: < 1°.

The change was small enough to miss in real time.

New orientation: Earth.

entries.title: THE MOON WAS IN ITS HAND
entries.caption:
We thought the Moon had drifted out of position.

It hadn't.

Something was holding it.

Earth was still visible below.

Too small to matter.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-007
entries.pinned_comment:
ARCHIVE NOTE:

The Moon was not falling.

It was not drifting.

The object around it was holding position.

entries.title: THE FIRST SIGNAL WAS A HEARTBEAT
entries.caption:
We thought the first signal was a transmission.

It wasn't carrying data.

It had a rhythm.

Then the second pulse arrived.

Same interval.
Same source.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-008
entries.pinned_comment:
SIGNAL NOTE:

The pulses were too regular for noise.

The next one arrived exactly when expected.

entries.title: THE SHADOW BEHIND JUPITER
entries.caption:
Jupiter should have hidden everything behind it.

Instead, something behind Jupiter made the planet look small.

We only saw the shadow move.

That was enough.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-009
entries.pinned_comment:
OBSERVATION NOTE:

The shadow did not match any known moon.

It crossed Jupiter's limb without changing shape.

Its full size remains unknown.

entries.title: THE OBJECT THAT BLOCKED THE SUN
entries.caption:
The Sun dimmed.

No eclipse was scheduled.
No planet crossed the disk.

Then the edge of the object came into focus.

It wasn't round.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-010
entries.pinned_comment:
SOLAR NOTE:

The obstruction moved too slowly for debris.

The corona traced an irregular surface.

It was not a planet.

entries.title: THE FACE INSIDE THE NEBULA
entries.caption:
We thought the nebula only looked like a face.

Then the clouds shifted.

The face stayed.

For one frame, the darkness inside it looked back.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-011
entries.pinned_comment:
IMAGE NOTE:

Cloud motion changed around the formation.

The structure did not.

Whatever made the shape was not moving with the gas.

entries.title: THE FINGER NEAR ORBIT
entries.caption:
Earth was never touched.

That is what made the frame worse.

The fingertip stopped just outside orbit.

Close enough to change every scale we understood.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-012
entries.pinned_comment:
ORBITAL NOTE:

No contact was recorded.

No impact followed.

The object simply remained there.

entries.title: THE WORLD THAT OPENED ITS EYE
entries.caption:
We catalogued it as a dead world.

Then a crack widened.

It wasn't a fault line.

It was an eyelid.

And it was still opening.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-013
entries.pinned_comment:
ARCHIVE NOTE:

The surface around the opening moved independently of the crust.

The eye continued to open.

entries.title: THE SIGNAL BENEATH SATURN
entries.caption:
Saturn's rings were quiet.

The signal wasn't coming from the planet.

It was coming from below it.

From a structure that should not have been there.

Then it pulsed again.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-014
entries.pinned_comment:
SIGNAL NOTE:

The source remained fixed beneath Saturn.

The pulse travelled through the structure before reaching our instruments.

entries.title: THE THING BEYOND MARS
entries.caption:
Mars was the closest object in the frame.

It still looked small.

The structure beyond it never approached.

It didn't have to.

We could not find where it ended.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-015
entries.pinned_comment:
DEPTH NOTE:

Mars provided the only usable scale reference.

The object behind it extended beyond the frame.

entries.title: THE STARS MOVED FIRST
entries.caption:
Nothing entered the system.

Nothing appeared on radar.

The stars moved first.

One line shifted.
Then another.

Only later did we see what they were bending around.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-016
entries.pinned_comment:
ASTROMETRY NOTE:

The displacement began before the object was visible.

The stars did not move together.

They moved around something.

entries.title: THE RING WAS NOT SATURN'S
entries.caption:
At first, we blamed the angle.

Then Saturn moved.

The second ring did not.

It was never Saturn's.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-017
entries.pinned_comment:
ORBITAL NOTE:

The two ring systems have different centers.

Only one belongs to Saturn.

entries.title: THE MOUTH BEYOND NEPTUNE
entries.caption:
Neptune was the last familiar object in the frame.

Beyond it, space opened.

Not like a door.
Not like a wound.

Like something waiting to inhale.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-018
entries.pinned_comment:
DEEP-FIELD NOTE:

Debris near the opening is moving inward.

No inner surface has been detected.

The depth reading never returned.

entries.title: THE HAND UNDER EARTH'S SHADOW
entries.caption:
We only saw the hand after Earth's shadow crossed it.

It was already there.

Below the planet.
Still.

Waiting in the dark.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-019
entries.pinned_comment:
SHADOW NOTE:

The structure did not emerge when the light changed.

The light only revealed what was already underneath.

entries.title: THE STAR THAT BLINKED BACK
entries.caption:
We aimed at a star.

The star brightened.
Then dimmed.
Then opened again.

The timing matched our observation window.

It blinked back.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-020
entries.pinned_comment:
STELLAR NOTE:

The event repeated once.

Same interval.

The second cycle began after observation started.

entries.title: SOMETHING SAT BEHIND THE SUN
entries.caption:
The Sun hid most of it.

That was the only reason we saw the outline.

Something enormous was sitting behind the light.

And it wasn't moving.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-021
entries.pinned_comment:
SOLAR OCCULTATION NOTE:

The silhouette remained fixed while the corona shifted around it.

Only a fraction of the structure was visible.

entries.title: EARTH HEARD IT BREATHE
entries.caption:
We never heard sound in space.

We detected a pattern.

One slow expansion.
Then another.

Earth's atmosphere answered each pulse.

Something out there was breathing.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-022
entries.pinned_comment:
ATMOSPHERIC NOTE:

The pulses arrived at regular intervals.

They were too slow to be mechanical.

Earth was inside the pattern.

entries.title: THE PLANET THAT WASN'T A PLANET
entries.caption:
We called it a planet because it was easier.

It had mass.
It had a horizon.

Then the seams lit up.

Planets do not have joints.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-023
entries.pinned_comment:
CLASSIFICATION NOTE:

Surface sections are moving independently.

The object is still listed as a planet.

That classification is no longer useful.

entries.title: IT WORE THE ECLIPSE
entries.caption:
The eclipse was perfect.

Too perfect.

Then the dark structure shifted.

The ring of light stayed centered on it.

It wasn't passing through the eclipse.

It was wearing it.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-024
entries.pinned_comment:
ECLIPSE NOTE:

The alignment remained stable after the surrounding field changed.

The corona continued to frame the same structure.

entries.title: THE EYE INSIDE JUPITER'S STORM
entries.caption:
Jupiter's storm had been turning long before we were watching.

Then one frame showed a pupil.

We checked the next frame.

It was wider.

The storm was opening its eye.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-025
entries.pinned_comment:
STORM NOTE:

The surrounding clouds continued rotating.

The central structure did not.

It was looking through the storm.

entries.title: IT FOLDED SPACE AROUND EARTH
entries.caption:
Earth did not move.

The space around it did.

Stars bent.
Distance collapsed.

For a moment, our planet was inside a fold.

Then the geometry relaxed.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-026
entries.pinned_comment:
GEOMETRY NOTE:

Earth's position was unchanged.

Only the path around it shortened.

We still do not know what caused the fold.

entries.title: THE MOON CHANGED ORBIT FOR IT
entries.caption:
The Moon changed orbit.

Not toward Earth.
Not away from it.

Toward something else.

Something our models did not include.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-027
entries.pinned_comment:
ORBITAL NOTE:

The deviation was small.

The correction persisted.

The Moon is now responding to another mass.

entries.title: THE SIGNAL CAME FROM BELOW
entries.caption:
We spent weeks searching the sky for the signal.

Wrong direction.

The source was below the surface.

And it had been transmitting upward the whole time.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-028
entries.pinned_comment:
SUBSURFACE NOTE:

The signal weakens as altitude increases.

The strongest reading comes from below the crust.

entries.title: IT FINALLY MOVED
entries.caption:
It had been motionless in every frame.

Every scan.
Every pass.

Then one section moved.

Barely.

The stars around it moved with it.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-029
entries.pinned_comment:
FINAL ARCHIVE NOTE:

This is the first confirmed movement.

No acceleration followed.

It only changed position once.

That was enough.
